conventions.convention: Proper means nonempty finite effective domain; closed means closed epigraph in Euclidean space. Convex combinations use 0·(+∞)=0 at endpoints.
The proximal mapping initially denotes a minimizer set for parameter t>0; after singleton existence is proved, the same notation denotes its unique member.
The η-subdifferential uses g(z)≥g(x)+〈p,z−x〉−η for every z, with η≥0; it is empty outside dom g.
Exact FISTA starts with t₁=1 and y₁=x₀, uses xₖ=T_L(yₖ), and extrapolates with coefficient (tₖ−1)/tₖ₊₁. Restart resets momentum and the previous iterate at each full block.
In the FISTA energy recurrence t₀=0, u₀=x₀−x*, and the k=1 previous objective term is interpreted as zero, including when F(x₀)=+∞.
An inexact call must return a finite-domain point with L(yₖ−xₖ)−∇f(yₖ)∈∂ηₖg(xₖ); failure to supply that certificate returns inconclusive.
Strong convexity is the strong-Jensen inequality on finite-domain pairs for 0<θ<1 and μ>0.
The normal cone is outward: 〈v,z−x〉≤0 for every z∈C. The projected-gradient theorem asserts fixed-point/normal-cone equivalence and KKT-multiplier sufficiency, without a multiplier converse.

load_bearing.statement: For proper closed convex g:Rⁿ→(−∞,+∞], every t>0 and v∈Rⁿ give a singleton prox_tg(v). Its member u satisfies u=prox_tg(v) iff (v−u)/t∈∂g(u). For uᵢ=prox_tg(vᵢ), ‖u₁−u₂‖²≤〈u₁−u₂,v₁−v₂〉; in particular the map is nonexpansive.
For convex continuously differentiable f:Rⁿ→R with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0, and proper closed convex g, put F=f+g and x⁺=T_L(y). For every z∈Rⁿ, F(z)≥F(x⁺)+(L/2)‖x⁺−y‖²+L〈y−z,x⁺−y〉.
Let n∈N and let g:Rⁿ→(−∞,+∞] be proper, closed and convex in the epigraph convention. Then there are a∈Rⁿ and b∈R such that g(x)≥〈a,x〉+b for every x∈Rⁿ.

Under the exact FISTA hypotheses with minimizer x*, set t₀=0, u₀=x₀−x*, and uₖ=tₖxₖ−(tₖ−1)xₖ₋₁−x*. For every k≥1, (2tₖ²/L)(F(xₖ)−F(x*))+‖uₖ‖²≤(2tₖ₋₁²/L)(F(xₖ₋₁)−F(x*))+‖uₖ₋₁‖², with the k=1 previous objective term interpreted as zero.

For convex continuously differentiable f with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0, and proper closed convex g, suppose L(y−x⁺)−∇f(y)∈∂ηg(x⁺), η≥0. With F=f+g, every z∈Rⁿ satisfies F(z)≥F(x⁺)+(L/2)‖x⁺−y‖²+L〈y−z,x⁺−y〉−η.

For certified inexact FISTA with errors ηₖ≥0 and minimizer x*, the exact FISTA energy recurrence holds with the additional right-hand term 2tₖ²ηₖ/L, using t₀=0, u₀=x₀−x*, uₖ=tₖxₖ−(tₖ−1)xₖ₋₁−x*, and a zero previous objective term at k=1.

alerts.finding: In thm-nearest-point-in-a-nonempty-closed-convex-set, Proof 1.1 says: “Choose c₀∈C and put R=‖x−c₀‖₂. The set K=C∩B̄(x,R) is nonempty, closed, and bounded”. The permitted choice c₀=x gives R=0, whereas def-metric-ball explicitly requires strictly positive radii and says “a ball of radius 0 or of negative radius is never written in this library.” The proof needs a separate R=0 case or a positive enclosing radius. This is an immediately closable boundary-case omission; the nearest-point statement remains sound.

seams_checked.note: The projected-gradient theorem preserves the outward normal sign, affine constraint setting, nonnegative multipliers and complementarity. It uses convex KKT sufficiency and explicitly declines a multiplier converse.
The normal-cone/projection-resolvent lemma uses the indicator, exact subgradient definition and positive-parameter proximal resolvent with their stated hypotheses.

The bundle consumers retain proper closed convex inputs and use exact proximal existence, nonexpansiveness and the zero-subgradient certificate. Their aggregate-model error argument is separate from the certified inexact FISTA model.

Block proximal calls use positive majorizers and proper closed convex penalties. Closedness arguments use epigraphs; existence arguments apply the affine-minorant and continuous-sum lemmas within their domains.

Conjugate properness uses the affine minorant; ADMM uses exact subgradient inequalities; PDHG uses positive-parameter proximal resolvents. General ADMM subproblem attainment is separately guarded rather than inferred from the proximal theorem.

Smooth descent is used without adding a convexity requirement to that supplier. Projected SGD uses indicator projection and nonexpansiveness; strong-convexity consumers retain the strong-Jensen inequality on their stated domains.

Finite-sum proofs use the stated smooth descent inequality and strong-convexity convention. AdaGrad reduces its positive diagonal metric subproblem to an ordinary Euclidean proximal problem after scaling.

The PDE algorithm references the proximal-gradient procedure but supplies its own finite-dimensional projection and approximate-gradient certificate contract. It does not import exact PG/FISTA objective rates for its inexact backend.
